The runtime

A workspace built as one graph.

Under the app is a runtime that gives every space, document, command and conversation an identity, and expresses every relation between them the same way. The app is a set of views over those objects and keeps no second copy of any of them. Four ideas carry most of it.

Identity

Nothing is copied.

Every object in Scint has one reference, and everything that uses the object holds that reference. A space points to its documents with one. A document points to a document inside it with one. A conversation points to the run behind a reply with one.

Nobody holds a copy, so nobody holds a stale one. When an agent edits a document you have open there is nothing to sync, because there is only one document.

A reference leaves Scint as a link and comes back as the same object, whether it travelled through a document, a command's arguments or another application. Remove an object and its name stays behind, so a link held elsewhere still says what it pointed to.

Structure

Where things belong, and how they relate.

A project needs a hierarchy and a web of connections, and forcing one into the other bends both. Scint keeps them as two structures over the same spaces. Containment says where a space belongs. Bridges say which spaces work together, and they cross the hierarchy freely.

A bridge is more than a line. It holds documents and commands of its own, so the relationship between two spaces carries what their collaboration runs on.

Documents

Content that runs.

Documents are built from blocks: headings, paragraphs, code, tasks, and references to files, commands and other documents. A block that refers to another document makes documents recursive. A brief can hold the research it depends on, and a second brief can hold the same research.

A request in Scint is a document too. Its first block records where it belongs and how it should run, so instructions travel with everything needed to carry them out. One model serves as a page you read, a request you send and a task that fires on a schedule.

Routing

One decision, then the work.

A space works in one intent at a time, and the intent decides what its agent sees. Choosing it is a decision, and Scint treats it as one. Each request goes to Jev, TypeSafe's decision model, which returns a single choice and a confidence. A confident choice switches the space. Anything less leaves the space as it was, and the request runs either way.

Routing costs one call and no agent turn. You type into one input for every kind of work.

Who built it

The runtime, the app and its design system are designed and built by one person, Tim Kaechle.

See it working

Your spaces and documents stay in files on your Mac. Routing sends the request and the last few messages of its thread to TypeSafe's Jev, and the agents you run talk to their own providers.
